units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
How do you do, Peter? What, still ill? How silly of you!
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: With evident pleasure, as he catches sight of MASHA.
How are you, Miss Masha?
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: So you recognised me?
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She shakes hands with him.
Did you marry him?
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Long ago.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: You are happy now?
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: He bows to DORN and MEDVIEDENKO, and then goes hesitatingly toward TREPLIEFF.
Your mother says you have forgotten the past and are no longer angry with me.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: TREPLIEFF gives him his hand.
To her son.
Here is a magazine that Boris has brought you with your latest story in it.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: To TRIGORIN, as he takes the magazine.
Many thanks; you are very kind.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Your admirers all send you their regards. Every one in Moscow and St. Petersburg is interested in you, and all ply me with questions about you. They ask me what you look like, how old you are, whether you are fair or dark. For some reason they all think that you are no longer young, and no one knows who you are, as you always write under an assumed name. You are as great a mystery as the Man in the Iron Mask.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: Do you expect to be here long?
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: No, I must go back to Moscow to-morrow. I am finishing another novel, and have promised something to a magazine besides. In fact, it is the same old business.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: During their conversation ARKADINA and PAULINA have put up a card-table in the centre of the room; SHAMRAEFF lights the candles and arranges the chairs, then fetches a box of lotto from the cupboard.

The weather has given me a rough welcome. The wind is frightful. If it goes down by morning I shall go fishing in the lake, and shall have a look at the garden and the spot--do you remember?--where your play was given. I remember the piece very well, but should like to see again where the scene was laid.
units.name: TRIGORIN

units.text: To her father.
Father, do please let my husband have a horse. He ought to go home.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Angrily.
A horse to go home with!
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Sternly.
You know the horses have just been to the station. I can’t send them out again.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: But there are other horses.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Seeing that her father remains silent.
You are impossible!
units.name: MASHA

units.text: I shall go on foot, Masha.
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: With a sigh.
On foot in this weather?
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: She takes a seat at the card-table.
Shall we begin?
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: It is only six miles. Good-bye.
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: He kisses his wife’s hand;.
Good-bye, mother.
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: His mother-in-law gives him her hand unwillingly.
I should not have troubled you all, but the baby--
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: He bows to every one.
Good-bye.
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: He goes out with an apologetic air.
He will get there all right, he is not a major-general.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: Come, let us begin. Don’t let us waste time, we shall soon be called to supper.
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: SHAMRAEFF, MASHA, and DORN sit down at the card-table.
